name: GreenSquareDC WAi1 data centre campus (Abernethy Road)
notes: GreenSquareDC's first WA campus at 37-39 Abernethy Road, Belmont: DCD (Oct 2022) reported a 96MW, AU$600m application lodged via Urbis; state planners (DAP pathway) approved the four-storey, ~68,000 sqm GFA data centre (perthnow, Oct 2022). In Aug 2023 GreenSquareDC leased adjacent land for a wind/solar park to power the Perth campus. No public evidence found that the Belmont campus reached construction or operation; datacentermap/ocolo list WAi1 at 96MW. Capacity is approved/ultimate campus capacity, not operational IT load.

name: Nexion W1 data centre
developer: Nexion Networks (sold to Carrier Connect Systems)
notes: Nexion W1 at 37-39 Robinson Avenue, Belmont: ~2MW, 8,000 sq ft facility. DCD reported Carrier Connect Systems' agreement to acquire the Perth facility; ASX announcement 2025-07-28 confirms completion of sale of Nexion's data centre to Carrier Connect with Nexion continuing to pay wholesale rack rental and a ~AUD$120k pa operations contract. Vocus WA-data-centres list places Nexion W1 at the Belmont address.

name: Project Meridien / Gingerah Energy Hub AI data centre
developer: Gingerah Energy / Karajarri Traditional Lands Association / Fugro / Longreach Capital Investment
notes: Project Meridien: renewable-powered AI training data centre on Karajarri country south of Broome (Kimberley), combining solar, wind, batteries and limited gas to reach up to ~1 GW ultimate. ABC News (2026-04-20) reports phase one of ~240 MW IT capacity, feasibility complete, FEED/environmental work next, FID targeted 2029, first-stage operations targeted 2032. Gingerah Energy and Royal HaskoningDHV (feasibility study) official pages confirm. Status planned/announced - no planning application lodged yet.

name: CipherTel Bunbury datacentre and managed backup facilities
notes: CipherTel official site: licensed Australian carrier, WA-owned, run from Bunbury, operating fixed-wireless/microwave/fibre networks and datacentre/backup services across multi-site Bunbury facilities. Business News lists CipherTel head office, network exchange, data centre and NOC in Bunbury with a second data centre in the Perth CBD.

name: City of Bunbury civic data centre / private cloud platform
developer: City of Bunbury / Stott + Hoare / IBM
notes: GovTechReview: City of Bunbury built a data centre and migrated 35+ legacy servers to IBM PureSystems/PureFlex with excess rack/compute/storage capacity for potential hosted council services. A 2008 WA Government release funded power/cooling infrastructure for the Bunbury digital centre's data centre. Small civic facility, no colocation market data.

name: ISA Technologies Bunbury data centre
notes: iTnews (2009): Perth-based ISA Technologies commissioned a Bunbury data centre as its third facility to support private/public cloud services alongside Perth and Kuala Lumpur sites. Current operating status and site-level capacity not confirmed in public sources; historical record only.
